 A win, but not a statement 
 By SAMMY BROOKS | Author of "The Game Within" Series 
 Nov 10, 2026 
 54 mins ago 
 0 
 Facebook 
 Twitter 
 WhatsApp 
 SMS 
 Email 
 Facebook 
 Twitter 
 WhatsApp 
 SMS 
 Email 
 Print 
 Copy article link 
 Save 
 The Cowboys won Sunday, and at this point I’ll take a win however we can get one. Dallas escaped Indianapolis with a 27-23 victory, moved to 4-5 and kept that wonderful little “still in the hunt” graphic alive for at least another week. 
 My question is whether this win actually changed anything. 
 The Colts came into the game at 2-6 and had lost four straight, yet Dallas still needed a late touchdown drive to avoid another fourth quarter collapse. Indianapolis took a 23-20 lead with less than two minutes remaining before Dak Prescott and the offense finally rescued the Cowboys with a game winning drive. 
 Thankfully, the offense continues to give me hope. 
 Dallas finished with 508 yards, Dak threw for 335 yards and two touchdowns, CeeDee Lamb went crazy with 10 catches for 195 yards and Javonte Williams added 101 rushing yards. When this offense is clicking, I genuinely believe it has enough firepower to compete with almost anybody. 
 That’s why I’m having a hard time believing the offense will be the reason this team misses the playoffs. 
 The defense did have a better day statistically, holding Indianapolis to 271 yards and ending the game with Caleb Downs intercepting Daniel Jones. I’ll give them credit for that, but I’m not suddenly convinced everything is fixed because we survived a struggling Colts team. 
 Through nine games, Dallas still sits near the bottom of the league defensively, allowing more than 370 yards per game. That’s the part I can’t get past when I try to picture this team making an actual playoff run. 
 If we’re having trouble closing out Daniel Jones and Indianapolis, what happens when Dallas runs into one of the better teams in the NFC? 
 The Cowboys are also extremely fortunate that the NFC East has left the door open. The Giants are in front, but Dallas is still close enough that a run could completely change the season. That means I’ll continue rooting against New York every chance I get, because at this point Cowboys fans need all the help we can get. 
 It honestly reminds me a little of the Rangers down the stretch this year. They weren’t some dominant baseball team, but a struggling division gave them an opportunity to make October anyway. 
 Dallas has been given a similar opportunity. 
 If the division is going to leave the door open, the Cowboys better be the team that walks through it. 
 I’m happy about Sunday’s win, and I’m certainly not giving up on the season. It’s just difficult to watch this team right now and envision a playoff run without seeing major improvement from the defense. 
 The Cowboys are still alive. 
 Whether that actually means anything is up to them. 
 Go Cowboys.
